articles.title: Association Between Weight Loss on Incretin-Based Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
articles.abstract: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo. A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects. Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%). Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: A Phase 2, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Acmopatide (CT-868), a Fully Biased GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist, in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Overweight or Obesity.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acmopatide, a signal-biased glucagon-like peptide 1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight/obesity. In this phase 2, 16-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study, adults with T1D (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%; BMI ≥27 kg/m2) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to once-daily subcutaneous acmopatide (1.8, 4.1, or 6.6 mg) or volume-matched placebo. The primary end point was change from baseline (CFB) in HbA1c (%) at week 16; secondary end points included percent CFB in body weight and insulin dose. Overall, 111 participants were randomized (placebo n = 29, acmopatide 1.8 mg n = 27, 4.1 mg n = 28, 6.6 mg n = 27). Mean (SD) baseline HbA1c was 7.5% (0.6), and mean BMI was 34.3 (5.6) kg/m2. Acmopatide improved HbA1c (least squares [LS] mean CFB -0.4 to -0.6% vs. -0.3% with placebo; nominally significant placebo-adjusted difference for 4.1 mg: -0.3% [90% CI -0.6 to -0.1]; P = 0.020). HbA1c <7.0% was achieved by 55.6% of participants receiving acmopatide 4.1 mg vs. 33.3% receiving placebo. Acmopatide-treated participants demonstrated reductions in body weight (LS mean CFB -3.3 to -6.7% vs. 0.3% with placebo; all P < 0.01), total daily insulin dose (-3.4 to -14.9% more than placebo for acmopatide 4.1 and 6.6 mg), and mean systolic blood pressure (-3.1 to -8.4 mmHg vs. -3.3 mmHg with placebo). Adverse events were primarily gastrointestinal. No diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or severe hypoglycemia events occurred. In adults with T1D and overweight/obesity, acmopatide was associated with improved glycemic control and clinically meaningful weight loss without DKA or severe hypoglycemia events.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of RCTs Using Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.
articles.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is a reasonable alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). We conducted an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC versus OAC in patients with AF. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/all-cause death. The primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. Secondary endpoints included net adverse clinical events, all-cause death, nonprocedure-related bleeding, and ischemic stroke. Reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis using a 2-stage approach and study-level meta-analysis using random-effects models were performed. Six trials enrolling 7,004 patients randomized to LAAC (n = 3,681) or OAC (n = 3,323) were included. There were no significant differences between LAAC versus OAC for the primary efficacy endpoint (difference in restricted mean survival time [∆RMST] -0.006 years, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.027 to 0.015 years, p = 0.56) or primary safety endpoint (∆RMST 0.004 years, 95% CI -0.025 to 0.034 years, p = 0.77) at 3 years. Nonprocedure-related bleeding was significantly lower with LAAC versus OAC (∆RMST 0.162 years, 95% CI 0.104 to 0.220 years, p <0.001) with no difference in all-cause death (∆RMST 0.029 years, 95% CI -0.031 to 0.089 years, p = 0.34). In a study-level meta-analysis, ischemic stroke was not significantly different with LAAC versus OAC (risk ratio 1.32, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.86, p = 0.09). In conclusion, the trade-off between a statistically significant lower risk of nonprocedure-related bleeding and a numerically, but not statistically, higher risk of ischemic stroke with LAAC versus OAC necessitates individualized risk assessment and shared decision-making for patients with AF at elevated risk of stroke.

articles.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
articles.abstract: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. articles.title: Fecal Immunochemical Test Outreach for Colorectal Cancer Screening in Community Health Centers: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening is suboptimal among people in traditionally underserved populations, many of whom receive primary care at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs). Mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) outreach improves screening, especially in underserved populations, but questions remain about impact over time. To evaluate the effectiveness of centralized annual mailed FIT outreach delivered over 3 years to increase CRC screening in FQHCs. This cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted between June 1, 2021, and May 31, 2024. Sixteen clinics from 2 FQHCs in Southern California were randomly assigned to mailed FIT outreach or usual care for patients aged 50 to 75 years and not up to date with screening. Intervention components followed best practices for mailed FIT outreach and included educational primers, FIT kits, and telephone reminders. The primary outcome was the proportion of individuals up to date with any CRC screening after 3 years of intervention (point prevalence); screening at 2 years was a secondary outcome. Due to a resource constraint-related protocol modification, mailed FIT outreach began earlier in year 3, such that some individuals who completed screening in year 2 were not yet due for repeat FIT. Among 16 clinics serving 20 250 patients, 6 clinics serving 8334 individuals at baseline (4435 aged 55-64 years [53.2%]; 4896 female [58.7%]; 341 Asian [4.1%], 238 Black [2.9%], 2390 Hispanic [28.7%], and 4371 non-Hispanic White [52.4%]) were randomized to intervention and 10 clinics serving 11 916 individuals at baseline (6443 aged 55-64 years [54.1%]; 7250 female [60.8%]; 699 Asian [5.9%], 355 Black [3.0%], 4635 Hispanic [38.9%], and 4436 non-Hispanic White [37.2%]) were randomized to usual care. At year 3, screening was 39.4% (95% CI, 36.3% to 42.6%) in intervention clinics vs 36.5% (95% CI, 31.2% to 42.2%) in usual care clinics, which was not a statistically significant difference (2.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.2 to 9.0 percentage points). At year 2, screening was 37.8% (95% CI, 35.2% to 40.4%) in intervention clinics vs 27.0% (95% CI, 21.8% to 32.9%) in usual care clinics (difference, 10.8 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.9 to 16.7 percentage points). This study's findings suggest that centralized mailed FIT outreach could increase CRC screening in FQHCs serving populations with persistent disparities, although maintaining intervention fidelity and providing ongoing implementation support over time are needed for consistent impact. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04941300.

articles.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting  messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

articles.title: Digital and Coaching Interventions for Uptake of Cancer Genetic Testing: The MiGHT Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Germline genetic testing (GT) for hereditary cancer risk can inform cancer treatment, screening, and prevention, yet testing rates remain low. Alternative strategies are needed to improve facilitation of GT. To compare 2 patient-level interventions to increase uptake of hereditary cancer GT against usual care. The Michigan Genetic Hereditary Testing (MiGHT) randomized clinical trial analyzed self-reported GT outcome data from participants meeting clinical GT criteria between April 21, 2022, and November 21, 2025. Participants were adults (age ≥18 years) who met national criteria for genetic evaluation and had not previously completed germline GT recruited from oncology, primary care, and gastroenterology practices; research registries; and the general public in Michigan. Data were analyzed from April 30, 2025, to May 1, 2026. Participants were randomized to either telephone-based health coaching, a self-directed digital intervention, or usual care. Both interventions incorporated genetics education and motivational interviewing concepts. GT uptake was assessed at 6- and 12-month time points. The primary outcome was completion of GT by 6 months. The effects of study group on GT uptake were evaluated using logistic regression, adjusting for cancer history, age, gender, and race. A total of 793 participants (median [IQR] age, 64 [51-71] years; 458 [57.8%] female) were randomized to health coaching (261 participants), the digital intervention (265 participants), or usual care (267 participants). Overall, 31 participants (4.9%) reported completing GT by the 6-month time point, and 76 participants (9.6%) underwent GT across the 12-month study period. Compared with usual care, participants in the digital intervention group had higher odds of completing GT by 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 3.88; 97.5% CI, 1.27-14.80), while those in the health coaching group had higher odds of completing GT by 12 months (AOR, 2.25; 97.5% CI, 1.11-4.77). Participants in the digital intervention group were more likely to express intention to test at 6 months (AOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.44-3.93), whereas those in the health coaching group had higher intention at both 6 (AOR, 2.99; 95% CI, 1.83-4.95) and 12 (AOR, 2.29; 95% CI 1.29-4.15) months compared with usual care. In this randomized clinical trial of GT interventions, GT uptake was higher among participants who received the digital or health coaching interventions compared with usual care, although overall testing rates were low. These results underscore the importance of content delivery, motivational messaging, and alternative GT care models. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05162846.

articles.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone. This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. articles.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement. Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design. articles.title: Remote multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment in community settings: multisite randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common among community-dwelling older adults and represents a pragmatic target for community-level intervention. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a scalable, remotely delivered multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment, integrated into community and primary care settings. This 6-month, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial was performed at two public health centres in South Korea, enrolling adults aged 60-80 years with cognitive impairment and preserved functional independence. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to a videoconference-based exercise and nutritional support programme or to usual health promotion services. The primary outcome was change in the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Korean version (MoCA-K) score at 6 months; secondary outcomes included cognitive, functional, physical performance, frailty and depressive measures at 6 and 12 months. Among 140 participants (mean age 75.0 years; 60% female), equal numbers were randomised to intervention and control groups. At 6 months, the intervention group showed greater improvement in MoCA-K scores compared to the control group [2.3 points; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.4-3.1], and the difference was sustained at 12 months (1.1 points; 95% CI 0.3-2.0). The intervention was also associated with improvements in functional status and frailty at both time points. No intervention-related adverse events were reported. A remotely delivered multicomponent intervention improved cognition, functional independence and frailty in older adults with cognitive impairment identified through community-based screening. These findings support the effectiveness of scalable interventions integrated into community and primary care settings, particularly when access to in-person care is limited. articles.title: Concentrated Exposure Therapy vs Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Given the high prevalence, chronicity, and associated disability of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), optimizing treatment is a global priority. The Bergen 4-day treatment (B4DT), a concentrated exposure-based intervention, may reduce treatment burden and improve access to evidence-based care. To evaluate the efficacy of B4DT compared with internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) in reducing OCD symptom severity. Single-center randomized controlled trial (1:1 allocation). Between May 8, 2024, and August 8, 2025, adults (aged 18 to 72 years) with OCD were enrolled and were followed up for 3 months. Key exclusion criteria included schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, acute suicidality, substance dependence, and recent psychopharmacological changes. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, 8 weeks (posttreatment), and 3 months (follow-up) by masked evaluators. Patients were randomized to B4DT (including preparatory sessions) or an 8-week unguided iCBT program. The primary outcome was the change in OCD symptom severity, measured by the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). Secondary outcomes included self-reported OCD (OCI-R), dysfunctional cognitions, quality of life, depressive symptoms, experiential avoidance, global functioning, self-esteem, and treatment satisfaction. A total of 253 individuals were screened, and 119 were enrolled after 53 were found to be ineligible and 81 declined to participate. Sixty of the 119 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 33.5 [10.1] years; 79 [66.4%] women) were assigned to B4DT and 59 to iCBT. The primary analysis included all randomized participants (intention-to-treat). B4DT was associated with significantly greater reductions in OCD symptoms (Y-BOCS) than iCBT, with large effects at posttreatment (mean [SE] difference, -7.9 [0.9]; 95% CI, -9.7 to -6.0; Hedges g, -1.6) and sustained effects at 3-month follow-up (mean [SE] difference, -5.6 [1.1]; 95% CI, -7.8 to -3.4; Hedges g, -1.0). Secondary outcomes consistently favored B4DT. Response and remission rates at 3-month follow-up were higher with B4DT (35 of 57 [61.4%] vs 11 of 44 [25.0%] and 24 of 57 [42.1%] vs 6 of 44 [13.6%], respectively). In this randomized clinical trial of 119 adults with OCD, B4DT was superior to iCBT in reducing OCD symptom severity, with sustained benefits. Its brief, concentrated format may represent a scalable strategy to improve access to effective OCD treatment globally. German Clinical Trials Register: DRKS00034236.

articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups. Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. articles.title: Home Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Gamified Cognitive Control Training for Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a home-based treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD), although its effects are typically small to moderate and inconsistently observed. Because tDCS may act synergistically with behavioral interventions, combining both approaches represents a promising strategy for developing more effective home-based treatments for MDD. To investigate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of home-based tDCS and concurrent gamified cognitive control training (CCT) in adults with MDD. This multicenter, double-masked, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial with follow-up at week 10, masking checks at 2 time points, and expectancy assessments was conducted at 3 university hospitals in Latvia, Germany, and Israel between June 22, 2021, and August 8, 2024. Participants included adults aged 18 to 65 years with MDD, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores of at least 13, and no or stable antidepressant medication. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to active tDCS (2 mA; anode F3, cathode F4) plus a gamified CCT or sham tDCS plus a sham game. Participants were asked to complete 30 home treatment sessions (30 minutes each) over 6 weeks with software-assisted electrode positioning. The primary outcome was feasibility, defined as completing at least 20 of 30 sessions with greater than 50% probability. The secondary outcome was efficacy, measured as change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores from baseline to week 6. Of 111 enrolled participants, 109 were included in the modified intention-to-treat sample (55 in the active group and 54 in the control group; mean [SD] age, 33.1 [10.6] years; 69 female [63.3%]). Feasibility criteria were met, with 86 participants (78.9%) completing at least 20 sessions (lower bound of 1-sided 95% CI, 71.5%). The MADRS scores improved significantly in both groups at week 6, indicating insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the mean change in MADRS score from baseline to 6 weeks between the 2 treatment groups (difference, 0.89 [95% CI, -1.37 to 3.15]; P = .44; Cohen d, 0.10 [95% CI, -0.15 to 0.34]). Results were similar at follow-up (week 10). Adverse events were balanced between groups. This RCT of home-based tDCS combined with CCT in adults with MDD was feasible and safe but did not demonstrate superior efficacy over the control condition. Future studies should refine the mechanistic alignment between stimulation and cognitive interventions to optimize treatment effects. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04953208.

articles.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I=62·9%; τ=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I=99·2%; τ=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I=97·8%; τ=0·156). Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. articles.title: Near-infrared Autofluorescence Probe Versus Visual Identification for Parathyroid Detection and Functional Preservation During Total Thyroidectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: To assess whether PTeye-guided identification increases the number of parathyroid glands (PGs) preserved in situ and reduces hypoparathyroidism compared with visual identification alone. Injury or inadvertent removal of PGs during thyroidectomy is the main cause of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. Reliance on visual inspection makes intraoperative PG identification difficult. Probe-based near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) systems such as PTeye provide real-time, tissue-specific feedback that may enhance PG detection and preservation. In this single-center, prospective, randomized trial, patients undergoing first-time total thyroidectomy were allocated to PTeye-assisted or visual PG identification. Procedures were performed by 2 senior and 3 junior surgeons. The primary outcome was the number of PGs identified. Secondary outcomes included inadvertent parathyroidectomy, autotransplantation, and transient and last follow-up hypoparathyroidism. Among 154 randomized patients (77 per group; mean age 53.4±14.3 y; 84.4% female), PTeye increased the mean number of PGs identified (3.81 vs. 2.73; P <0.001) and the proportion with 3-4 PGs preserved in situ (98.7% vs. 87.0%; P =0.004). Inadvertent parathyroidectomy was less frequent with PTeye (5.2% vs. 20.8%; P =0.004). Junior surgeons performed more autotransplantations than senior surgeons when using PTeye (33.3% vs. 10.5%; P =0.015). Female sex ( P =0.047), ≤2 PGs preserved ( P =0.008), and autotransplantation ( P =0.010) predicted low postoperative day-1 parathormone serum level. Among junior surgeons, transient hypoparathyroidism was lower with PTeye (20.5% vs. 55.2%; P <0.001), with no difference among senior surgeons. Permanent hypoparathyroidism rates were similar between groups. PTeye-guided NIRAF improves PG identification and in situ preservation and reduces transient hypoparathyroidism, particularly for junior surgeons, without affecting permanent hypoparathyroidism.

articles.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjogren's Disease.
articles.abstract: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor. We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48. Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups. In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

articles.title: Imaging for diagnosis, monitoring and outcome prediction in polymyalgia rheumatica: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis informing an international task force.
articles.abstract: To summarise evidence on imaging for the diagnosis, monitoring and outcome prediction in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) to inform an international task force. Six research questions across diagnostic, monitoring, prognostic and technical aspects were defined. A systematic literature review searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, Epistemonikos and the Cochrane Library (through July 2025), including prospective and retrospective cohort studies (≥20 patients) as well as case–control and cross-sectional studies for diagnostic aspects. Test performance was summarised descriptively and meta-analysed using bivariate random-effects models when ≥2 low or some concerns on risk-of-bias (RoB) studies were available. Forty-nine studies were included: 32 on diagnosis, 6 on monitoring, 13 on outcome prediction and 8 on technical aspects (some studies covered ≥1 aspect). No study was graded as low RoB. Diagnostic studies identified useful imaging lesions (eg, extracapsular and bilateral inflammatory patterns of shoulders and hips), but few were validated in independent cohorts. Diagnostic accuracy of positron emission tomography scores was reduced in the case of prior treatment and when used to differentiate PMR from other inflammatory diseases. Glucocorticoids substantially reduced sensitivity across modalities, highlighting the value of timely imaging when indicated. Data on monitoring and outcome prediction were sparse and heterogeneous. This systematic literature review serves as a basis for the formulation of international recommendations on the use of imaging in PMR. Available evidence was heterogeneous and of limited quality but revealed distinct imaging lesions and scores that can support PMR diagnosis. Well-designed prospective studies and external validations are needed.

articles.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Metformin is increasingly used to treat gestational diabetes mellitus and other insulin-resistant conditions during pregnancy. Because it crosses the placenta, concerns remain regarding its potential effects on offspring growth and metabolic programming. This systematic review evaluated the effects of prenatal metformin exposure on infant nutritional status and adiposity during the first year of life. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care during pregnancy. Eligible studies reported infant nutritional status or adiposity-related outcomes from birth to 12 months. Risk of bias was assessed, and results were synthesized narratively. Eight publications from six randomized controlled trials were included. Birthweight and birth size classifications were the most frequently reported outcomes. Metformin was not consistently associated with differences in birthweight or other anthropometric measures. One trial reported lower birthweight, while two reported fewer large-for-gestational-age or macrosomic infants. No study assessed direct measures of infant adiposity. Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes and Recovery After Robot-Assisted vs Open Radical Hysterectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the RACC Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Minimally invasive radical hysterectomy was introduced to reduce perioperative morbidity in early-stage cervical cancer, but concerns regarding oncologic safety have limited its use. High-quality prospective randomized data evaluating perioperative safety and recovery after robot-assisted radical hysterectomy remain limited. To compare perioperative safety and health-related quality of life (HRQOL) after robot-assisted vs open radical hysterectomy. The Robot-Assisted Approach to Cervical Cancer (RACC) trial, a multicenter, noninferiority, phase 3 randomized clinical trial, was conducted at tertiary centers in Europe. Female participants aged 18 years and older with cervical cancer (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics [FIGO] 2018 stage IB [excluding IB3] or IIA1) were enrolled. Patients were randomized between 2019 and 2025. Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical hysterectomy. Prespecified secondary outcomes included intraoperative complications (graded using standardized classification systems), postoperative complications within 30 days (Clavien-Dindo), and HRQOL at 1 month (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30, European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Cervical Cancer Module, and EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level questionnaire). These prespecified secondary analyses were exploratory and were not powered for confirmatory inference. Of 900 randomized patients (robotic surgery, median [IQR] age, 46 [39-53] years; open surgery, median [IQR] age, 45 [37-54] years), 809 (90%) were included in the intraoperative safety analysis, 798 (89%) in the postoperative safety analysis, and 723 (80%) in the 1-month HRQOL analysis. Intraoperative complications occurred in 24 of 419 patients (5.7%) in the robot-assisted group vs 39 of 390 patients (10.0%) in the open surgery group (risk difference, -4.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -8.0 to -0.6 percentage points); most were minor, whereas major complications were infrequent and similar. Postoperative complications within 30 days were similar (33.4% vs 34.8%; risk difference, -1.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.9 to 5.2 percentage points), including readmission and reoperation. At 1 month, robot-assisted surgery was associated with small differences in selected domains, including physical functioning (+5 points; 95% CI, 3-8 points), role functioning (+8 points; 95% CI, 4-13 points), and lower pain (+5 points; 95% CI, 2-9 points), whereas most domains did not meet thresholds for clinically important differences. Results of this secondary analysis of the RACC randomized clinical trial show that robot-assisted radical hysterectomy was associated with fewer intraoperative complications, primarily reflecting lower-grade events, with similar postoperative morbidity compared with open surgery. Differences in early HRQOL were small, and overall findings indicate no improvement in clinically consequential postoperative outcomes or recovery. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03719547.

articles.title: Association Between Systemic Fluoroquinolones and Risk of Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone use has been associated with peripheral neuropathy in case reports, but there have been few noninterventional studies validating this association, and causality is unclear. The aim of this study was to estimate the association between systemic fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy relative to a comparator class of antibiotics, cephalosporins, using multiple databases to increase precision and assess the robustness of the results. Cohort studies were conducted using data from 2 databases of UK electronic primary care records, Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and GOLD, from April 1, 1997, to December 31, 2019. Among adults (age ≥18 years) without diabetes mellitus or previously recorded peripheral neuropathy prescribed systemic fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins, hazard ratios were estimated between fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy within 60 days of prescription using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighted Cox regression. Hazard ratios were similarly estimated for a positive control outcome of incident tendon rupture within 60 days of prescription. Risk differences for peripheral neuropathy were estimated using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator. Estimates were pooled across databases using fixed-effects meta-analysis. In total, 2,933,982 individuals prescribed fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins in Aurum (63.7% [n = 1,868,793] female; median age 49.5 years [interquartile range (IQR) 34.1-67.5]) and 995,457 in GOLD (63.5% [n = 632,033] female, median age 51.5 years [IQR 35.6-68.0]) were included. Of these individuals, at first treatment episode, 1,002,004 (34.2%) in Aurum and 381,734 (38.3%) in GOLD were prescribed fluoroquinolones. The estimated association between fluoroquinolones and peripheral neuropathy was close to the null at first treatment episode (pooled adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.20) and over all treatment episodes (pooled aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.92-1.20). Hazard ratios were elevated for a positive control outcome of tendon rupture at first treatment episode (pooled aHR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53) and over all treatment episodes (1.76, 95% CI 1.52-2.04). Findings were not indicative of a substantive difference in risk of peripheral neuropathy between those prescribed fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins. Potential residual confounding is a study limitation. Study results provide some reassurance to clinicians regarding risk of peripheral neuropathy with fluoroquinolones relative to a comparator antibiotic.

articles.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. articles.title: AGA/AASLD Clinical Practice Guideline on Management of Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
articles.abstract: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease associated with progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, liver transplantation, and premature mortality. Despite effective therapies, important challenges remain in the diagnosis and management of PBC, including identification of antimitochondrial antibody-negative disease, assessment of response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), risk stratification, treatment of patients with inadequate response, management of cholestatic pruritus, and prevention of recurrent disease after liver transplantation. The aim of this guideline was to develop evidence-based recommendations addressing these key areas of clinical care. The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) convened a multidisciplinary panel to develop clinical practice recommendations for adults with PBC. Systematic reviews were performed for 6 prioritized clinical questions. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to prioritize clinical outcomes and assess evidence, and its Evidence to Decision Framework was used to develop recommendations. The guideline panel agreed on 6 recommendations. These recommendations address the use of PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies in antimitochondrial antibody-negative suspected PBC, UDCA as first-line therapy, liver stiffness measurement for prognostication, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA, linerixibat for moderate to severe pruritus, and UDCA prophylaxis post-transplantation to reduce disease recurrence. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low. The guideline emphasizes early diagnosis, optimization of first-line therapy, risk-based treatment escalation, symptom management, and prevention of post-transplantation disease recurrence to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).
articles.abstract: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies. Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. 18 Dutch community hospitals. Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted. The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies. 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24). Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice. www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

articles.title: Efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of a nine-valent vaccine (ExPEC9V) for the prevention of invasive Escherichia coli disease in older adults: a phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (E.mbrace).
articles.abstract: Invasive Escherichia coli disease (IED) caused by extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) can lead to bacteraemia and sepsis. ExPEC9V is a conjugate vaccine targeting nine E coli O-serotypes that account for most E coli bloodstream infections. We aimed to evaluate ExPEC9V for safety, immunogenicity, and prevention of IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in adults aged 60 years and older. In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study conducted at 332 clinical sites in 20 countries (E.mbrace), we enrolled participants aged 60 years and older in stable health and with a history of urinary tract infection (UTI) within the previous 2 years. Participants were randomly assigned (in blocks of no set size with the use of interactive web response system, stratified by age and presence or absence of risk factors for complicated UTI) 1:1 to receive a single dose of intramuscular ExPEC9V or placebo. Participants, study-site personnel, and investigators remained masked to group allocation throughout the study. The primary endpoint was first IED in blood or sterile sites caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in the per-protocol efficacy analysis set (all randomly assigned, vaccinated participants without major protocol deviations); secondary endpoints included immunogenicity assessment in a subset of participants. Safety endpoints included solicited (safety subset), unsolicited (full analysis set), and serious (full analysis set) adverse events. A prespecified futility analysis conducted when at least 40% of the expected 53 IED events had occurred indicated lack of efficacy, leading to early study termination. We present final study results (data up to the date of the futility announcement), when 17 701 of the planned 19 800 participants had been vaccinated. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04899336). Participants were enrolled between June 30, 2021, and Feb 13, 2025. Of 18 844 individuals assessed for eligibility, 17 701 were enrolled, randomly assigned, and vaccinated (8858 with ExPEC9V and 8843 with placebo). The per-protocol efficacy included 17 637 participants (8822 for ExPEC9V and 8815 for placebo). There were 24 IED cases (11 in vaccine and 13 in placebo groups) caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in blood or sterile sites, yielding a vaccine efficacy of 14·63% (95% CI -106·57 to 65·38), indicating no protective effect. ExPEC9V had an acceptable safety profile, with more frequent low-grade adverse events in the ExPEC9V versus placebo group, balanced serious adverse event distribution among both groups, and no vaccine-related deaths. In this large phase 3 trial of older adults, ExPEC9V did not demonstrate efficacy in preventing first IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes, despite generating robust and sustained antibody responses. Development of the ExPEC9V vaccine has been discontinued. Johnson & Johnson and Sanofi.

articles.title: Non-antibiotic interventions to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in women: overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs), that is, ≥2 urinary tract infections (UTIs) in the past 6 months or ≥3 in the past 12 months, are common, have a substantial impact on quality of life, and cause major antibiotic use. To identify non-antibiotic interventions for prevention of rUTIs that have been assessed in systematic reviews, exploring their effectiveness, acceptability, and adherence. An overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on non-pharmaceutical and pharmaceutical (non-antibiotic) interventions for preventing rUTIs in women. Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Google Scholar, and Cochrane from January 2014 to May 2025 were searched for systematic reviews of RCTs assessing the effectiveness of community-based non-antibiotic interventions for preventing UTI in women aged ≥16 years with rUTIs. Studies in intensive care units, relating to people with indwelling catheters, or comparing different oral antibiotic regimens were excluded. There were no limitations regarding outcome measures or language. In total, 27 systematic reviews met inclusion criteria evaluating probiotics ( = 9), D-mannose ( = 7), vaginal oestrogen ( = 7), cranberry ( = 6), methenamine hippurate ( = 3), herbal medicine ( = 3), increased fluid intake ( = 2), systemic oestrogen ( = 4), acupuncture ( = 2), and vaccines ( = 2). Eight examined combination strategies. Cranberry and methenamine hippurate use are supported by systematic reviews, as is vaginal oestrogen among postmenopausal women, although questions remain around dose, duration, and treatment adherence. Reviews of probiotics, D-mannose, herbal medicine, acupuncture, and vaccines concluded that stronger evidence is needed. Increased fluid intake benefits women with low intake, but further research is needed on optimal intake. There was little information on treatment adherence or acceptability for many interventions. For effective interventions, questions remain about promoting adherence (vaginal oestrogen), or optimal preparation (cranberry), or duration (methenamine). For other interventions a stronger evidence base is needed.

articles.title: Antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an individual patient data network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials demonstrated that in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and a P2Y12 inhibitor reduce bleeding compared with vitamin K antagonist (VKA) plus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with no increase in ischemic risk; however, important gaps in knowledge remain, limiting certainty and generalizability of these findings. In this patient-level meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with AF undergoing PCI, Cox proportional hazard models, stratified by trial, were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (HR, 95%CI). articles.title: Predictors of Type 2 Diabetes Remission and Relapse After Metabolic-Bariatric Surgery or Medical-Lifestyle Therapy in the ARMMS-T2D Study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS) is effective in promoting remission of type 2 diabetes, but this outcome is not universally achieved. We identified baseline patient characteristics that predict diabetes remission and subsequent relapse after various MBS procedures versus intensive medical-lifestyle intervention. Alliance of Randomized Trials of Medicine vs. Metabolic Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes (ARMMS-T2D) is a 14-year, multicenter study of health outcomes in 262 patients with type 2 diabetes (68% women, age 49.9 ± 8.3 years, BMI 36.4 ± 3.5 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.5 ± 1.5%) previously randomized to MBS (n = 166) or medical-lifestyle management (n = 96). Predictors of remission (defined as HbA1c <6.5% on no glucose-lowering medications) and relapse were determined using univariate time-to-event analyses of prespecified candidate predictors plus agnostic, multivariate least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. Throughout a median of 11 years (maximum 14 years) of follow-up, 58% of participants randomized to MBS achieved diabetes remission versus 3% with medical-lifestyle management. Predictors of diabetes remission in univariate analyses included shorter diabetes duration, no insulin use, fewer glucose-lowering medication classes used, greater body weight, higher fasting C-peptide and insulin levels, and weight loss at 1 year (all P < 0.05). Diabetes remission predictors in multivariate analyses included baseline diabetes duration, insulin use, and weight change at 1 year (all P < 0.01). Diabetes relapse after initial remission in the MBS group was predicted by longer baseline diabetes duration and greater number of glucose-lowering medication classes used. Baseline predictors of diabetes remission and subsequent relapse among participants randomized to one of three MBS procedures or a medical-lifestyle intervention should help inform personalized selection of diabetes treatment.

Safety of withdrawal of pharmacological treatment after recovery from HER2 therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: the HER-SAFE trial.
articles.abstract: Heart failure therapy (HFT) is routinely continued in breast cancer survivors after recovery from anti-HER2 cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), despite limited evidence. HER-SAFE is the first randomised trial to assess HFT withdrawal in this population. In this open-label, multicentre, randomised controlled trial, breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD (asymptomatic, left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥50%, normalised biomarkers) were randomised to HFT withdrawal or continuation. Antecedent CTRCD was mild (relative global longitudinal strain [GLS] decline >15%, LVEF ≥50%), moderate (LVEF fall >10% to <50%), or severe (LVEF <40%). The primary endpoint was a moderate or severe CTRCD event over 12 months analysed by intention to treat; secondary endpoints included serial cardiac function, biomarkers, and quality of life. Between July 2023 and June 2025, 90 patients were randomised (all female; median age 50 years [IQR 43-59]; median 17.3 months [IQR 7.7-33.2] since CTRCD recovery; HFT predominantly renin-angiotensin system inhibitors [98%] and beta-blockers [88%]) - 46 randomised to HFT withdrawal (1 lost to follow-up) and 44 to continuation. The primary endpoint occurred in 1 of 45 with withdrawal (moderate asymptomatic CTRCD) versus 0 of 44 with continuation (between-group difference 2.2pp; 90% CI upper limit 9.4pp). No cardiovascular deaths, heart failure hospitalisations or symptomatic CTRCD occurred. Cardiac magnetic resonance-derived LVEF remained stable in both arms at 12 months (between-group difference -0.8% [-2.0 to +0.4], p=0.21). Among breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD, HFT withdrawal was not associated with symptomatic events or significant between-group difference in LVEF at 12-months.

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy - Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis.
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. articles.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.
articles.abstract: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain. We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days. A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group). In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

articles.abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain. We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety. A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively. Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

articles.title: Acupuncture for older adults with dementia in residential care homes: an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Dementia harms the mental health of older adults and poses a significant caregiver burden. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture in managing cognitive decline and related symptoms in older adults with dementia. Eligible participants were recruited from 19 local residential care homes for older people in Hong Kong, China, from 5 October 2021 to 27 August 2024, in an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial. 118 participants were randomised to acupuncture and care-as-usual control (n=59 in each group) for 12 weeks. The analyses were on the intention-to-treat population. The primary outcome was the mean baseline-to-endpoint change of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included the functional independence, pain, depressive and sleep symptoms. 85.6% (101/118) of participants completed the study. The primary outcome, MoCA, was not significantly improved in week 12. Subgroup analyses showed that the treatment effect on MoCA appeared to differ across dementia severity strata. Acupuncture was superior over control in improving functional independence (the Chinese version of the Modified Barthel Index, mean difference=4.12, 95% confidence interval=0.81, 7.44, P=0.015; standardised effect size=0.29). All treatment-related adverse events were mild, and 2 nontreatment-related death cases were reported. While no significant effect in cognitive function was observed, acupuncture was associated with an improvement in functional independence, and the treatment effect on cognition might differ across dementia severity strata. This warrants further validation of the exploratory results, identifying a subpopulation of older adults with dementia who could gain more benefits from acupuncture in improving cognitive function. www.ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04305951, date of registration: 10/03/2020.

articles.title: Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.
articles.abstract: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. articles.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups. Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg.
